Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

I’m here phrase

also here I am, present

classical

Hīc sum.

Other words

  • Ecce mē! — here I am!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 241b; Plaut. Epid. 5.2.15 (Lewis & Short); Traupman p. 100

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Lewis & Short (s.v. ecce): “here I am”; the answer in hide-and-seek.

  • Adsum. — I’m here, present; at your service

    first person of adsum · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 1031: Adsum, imperā, sī quid vīs.

    The answer to one’s name, and to a call for help.

Examples

  • Dīc ubi es? … ubi es? — Ecce mē. accēde ad mē atque adī contrā.

    Say where you are? … where are you? — Here I am; come to me, come this way.Plaut. Rud. 238–242

  • Adsum, imperā, sī quid vīs.

    Here I am; give your orders, if you want anything.Plaut. Mil. 1031

See also I’m with you, comfort, look!.

SourcesThe phrase is composed; the grouped card gave no source.
